definition: A substance that donates protons (H⁺) in solution (Brønsted–Lowry) or accepts an electron pair (Lewis).
The minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to occur.
example: A catalyst lowers the activation energy.

definition: A base that dissolves in water, producing hydroxide ions (OH⁻).
A saturated hydrocarbon containing only C–C single bonds; general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing at least one C=C double bond; general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
Different structural forms of the same element in the same physical state.
example: Diamond and graphite (carbon); O₂ and O₃

definition: A negatively charged ion, formed when an atom gains electrons.
The electrode where oxidation takes place.
The smallest particle of an element that keeps its chemical identity; a nucleus surrounded by electrons.
The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom (symbol Z).
The number of particles in one mole: 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
A substance that accepts protons (H⁺) or donates an electron pair.
The temperature at which a liquid's vapour pressure equals the surrounding pressure, so it boils.
A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up, by providing a route with lower activation energy.
The electrode where reduction takes place.
A positively charged ion, formed when an atom loses electrons.
An attraction that holds atoms or ions together in a substance.
A substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
The amount of solute in a given volume of solution, often in mol/dm³ (M).
A shared pair of electrons between two atoms.
A reaction in which one substance breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
Mass per unit volume (ρ = m/V).
Separating liquids by boiling and condensing them, based on different boiling points.
Decomposing a compound by passing an electric current through it when molten or dissolved.
A subatomic particle with a charge of −1 and very small mass, found in shells around the nucleus.
The arrangement of electrons in an atom's orbitals.
The ability of an atom to attract the shared electrons in a covalent bond.
example: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

definition: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom (all with the same atomic number).
A process that absorbs heat from the surroundings (ΔH > 0).
The heat content of a system at constant pressure; changes are written ΔH.
The state of a reversible reaction where forward and backward rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.
A process that releases heat to the surroundings (ΔH < 0).
A group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.
A vertical column of the periodic table; elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons.
An element of group 17: F, Cl, Br, I, At, Ts.
A compound containing only carbon and hydrogen.
A strong intermolecular attraction between an H atom bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on another N, O or F.
A substance that changes colour depending on pH.
An atom or group of atoms with an electric charge.
Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms.
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
The total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus (symbol A).
The temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid.
Two or more substances physically combined, not chemically bonded.
The mass of one mole of a substance, in g/mol.
The SI unit of amount of substance; contains 6.022 × 10²³ particles.
Two or more atoms covalently bonded together.
The reaction of an acid with a base to form a salt and water.
A neutral subatomic particle found in the nucleus, with mass ≈ 1 u.
An element of group 18, with a full outer shell and very low reactivity.
Loss of electrons (or increase in oxidation state).
A horizontal row of the periodic table.
A measure of acidity: pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]. Below 7 is acidic, 7 neutral, above 7 basic (at 25 °C).
A large molecule made of many repeating units (monomers).
An insoluble solid formed when two solutions react.
A positively charged subatomic particle in the nucleus.
A reaction in which reduction and oxidation happen together.
Gain of electrons (or decrease in oxidation state).
An ionic compound formed when the hydrogen of an acid is replaced by a metal or ammonium ion.
The substance that dissolves in a solvent.
The substance in which a solute dissolves.
The calculation of quantities of reactants and products using balanced equations.
A change directly from solid to gas without becoming liquid.
Electrons in the outermost shell, involved in bonding.
